claim: MicroED is a recently developed method that uses electron diffraction for structure determination from very small three-dimensional crystals of biological material.
source: MicroED is a recently developed method that uses electron diffraction for structure determination from very small three-dimensional crystals of biological material.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about MicroED presented in the abstract, supported by the entire manuscript describing the method.

claim: The structure of lysozyme was previously determined at 2.9 Å resolution with MicroED using a series of still diffraction patterns.
source: Previously we used a series of still diffraction patterns to determine the structure of lysozyme at 2.9 Å resolution with MicroED (Shi et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Shi et al., 2013).

claim: The structure of bovine liver catalase was determined from a single crystal at 3.2 Å resolution by MicroED.
source: Here we present the structure of bovine liver catalase determined from a single crystal at 3.2 Å resolution by MicroED.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the manuscript, supported by experimental data presented throughout.

claim: The MicroED data for catalase were collected by continuous rotation of the sample under constant exposure.
source: The data were collected by continuous rotation of the sample under constant exposure and were processed and refined using standard programs for X-ray crystallography.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used, which is detailed in the methods section.

claim: MicroED data can be processed and refined using standard programs for X-ray crystallography.
source: The data were collected by continuous rotation of the sample under constant exposure and were processed and refined using standard programs for X-ray crystallography.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the methods described in the manuscript where MOSFLM, POINTLESS, AIMLESS, and other X-ray crystallography programs were used.

claim: Bovine liver catalase has long resisted atomic analysis by traditional electron crystallography.
source: The ability of MicroED to determine the structure of bovine liver catalase, a protein that has long resisted atomic analysis by traditional electron crystallography, demonstrates the potential of this method for structure determination.
evidence: This is supported by historical context provided in the introduction regarding decades of unsuccessful attempts.

claim: In the original MicroED proof of concept paper, electron diffraction data were collected from stationary lysozyme microcrystals and the structure was determined to 2.9 Å resolution from a series of still diffraction patterns.
source: In the original MicroED proof of concept paper (Shi et al., 2013), electron diffraction data were collected from stationary lysozyme microcrystals and the structure was determined to 2.9 Å resolution from a series of still diffraction patterns.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the original MicroED paper.

claim: The MicroED method was substantially improved by employing 'continuous rotation' where data were recorded as the crystals were continuously rotated.
source: The method was substantially improved by employing 'continuous rotation' where data were recorded as the crystals were continuously rotated, resulting in higher quality data and allowing simple integration with existing processing programs used for X-ray crystallography (Nannenga et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior publication describing the improvement.

claim: Continuous rotation resulted in higher quality data and allowed simple integration with existing processing programs used for X-ray crystallography.
source: The method was substantially improved by employing 'continuous rotation' where data were recorded as the crystals were continuously rotated, resulting in higher quality data and allowing simple integration with existing processing programs used for X-ray crystallography (Nannenga et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation and demonstrated in the current work.

claim: The structure of lysozyme was determined to 2.5 Å resolution with improved statistics and data quality using continuous rotation MicroED relative to the original lysozyme MicroED study.
source: This led to the structure of lysozyme being determined to 2.5 Å resolution with improved statistics and data quality relative to the original lysozyme MicroED study.
evidence: This is a comparison to prior work, supported by citation context.

claim: Catalase is a more difficult target than lysozyme because it has a much larger unit cell, lower symmetry, and four molecules in the asymmetric unit.
source: Catalase is a more difficult target than lysozyme, because it has a much larger unit cell, lower symmetry, and four molecules in the asymmetric unit.
evidence: This is based on established crystallographic knowledge about what makes structure determination more challenging.

claim: Each catalase monomer contains one heme group as well as a bound NADP molecule.
source: Moreover, each catalase monomer contains one heme group as well as a bound NADP molecule (Fita and Rossmann, 1985).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior structural work on catalase.

claim: Catalase is one of the earliest samples studied by EM.
source: Catalase is one of the earliest samples studied by EM, but despite extensive efforts spanning decades, the 3D structure of catalase has not been solved using electron diffraction.
evidence: This is historical context supported by the citations that follow.

claim: Despite extensive efforts spanning decades, the 3D structure of catalase has not been solved using electron diffraction prior to this work.
source: Catalase is one of the earliest samples studied by EM, but despite extensive efforts spanning decades, the 3D structure of catalase has not been solved using electron diffraction.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to historical attempts.

claim: Catalase crystals have variable thicknesses with 6–10 protein layers reported.
source: This is because the crystals have variable thicknesses (6–10 protein layers have been reported [Dorset and Parsons, 1975b]), and therefore these crystals were not suitable for 3D structure determination by traditional electron crystallography procedures (Longley, 1967; Matricardi et al., 1972; Unwin, 1975; Unwin and Henderson, 1975; Dorset and Parsons, 1975a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior characterization of catalase crystals.

claim: Catalase crystals with variable thicknesses were not suitable for 3D structure determination by traditional electron crystallography procedures.
source: This is because the crystals have variable thicknesses (6–10 protein layers have been reported [Dorset and Parsons, 1975b]), and therefore these crystals were not suitable for 3D structure determination by traditional electron crystallography procedures (Longley, 1967; Matricardi et al., 1972; Unwin, 1975; Unwin and Henderson, 1975; Dorset and Parsons, 1975a).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior unsuccessful attempts.

claim: The analysis from crystal growth to final structural refinement took a total of 3 weeks.
source: This is an important next step for the MicroED method as the analysis was rapid, taking a total of 3 weeks from crystal growth to final structural refinement, and used data from only a single catalase microcrystal.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the timeline of the experimental work.

claim: The catalase structure determination used data from only a single catalase microcrystal.
source: This is an important next step for the MicroED method as the analysis was rapid, taking a total of 3 weeks from crystal growth to final structural refinement, and used data from only a single catalase microcrystal.
evidence: This is stated explicitly and supported by the data collection details.

claim: Catalase readily forms thin 3D microcrystals which can be analyzed by transmission electron microscopy.
source: Catalase was chosen for this study as it readily forms thin 3D microcrystals, which can be analyzed by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) (Sumner and Dounce, 1937; Dorset and Parsons, 1975a; Baker et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on catalase crystallization.

claim: Well-ordered catalase microcrystals were grown by solubilizing crystalline catalase from an aqueous suspension followed by overnight dialysis in 0.05 M Sodium phosphate, pH 6.3.
source: Well-ordered catalase microcrystals were grown by solubilizing crystalline catalase from an aqueous suspension followed by overnight dialysis in 0.05 M Sodium phosphate, pH 6.3.
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure used in this study.

claim: The average crystal dimensions were found to be on the order of 8 µm by 4 µm in length and width and approximately 150 nm thick.
source: The average crystal dimensions were found to be on the order of 8 µm by 4 µm in length and width and approximately 150 nm thick, in good agreement with previous crystallization results (Dorset and Parsons, 1975b).
evidence: This is a measurement from the experimental data.

claim: The measured crystal dimensions are in good agreement with previous crystallization results.
source: The average crystal dimensions were found to be on the order of 8 µm by 4 µm in length and width and approximately 150 nm thick, in good agreement with previous crystallization results (Dorset and Parsons, 1975b).
evidence: This compares current measurements to prior literature.

claim: Well-ordered crystals showed sharp reflections extending to approximately 3.0 Å for untilted crystals.
source: Suitable crystals were assessed by collecting a single still diffraction pattern at a total dose of 0.05 e−/Å2, where well-ordered crystals showed sharp reflections extending to approximately 3.0 Å for untilted crystals (Figure 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the diffraction data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Well-embedded and relatively flat crystals yielded data to ∼2.8 Å resolution untilted but only ∼3.2 Å at high tilt.
source: Typically, well-embedded and relatively flat crystals yielded data to ∼2.8 Å resolution untilted but only ∼3.2 Å at high tilt.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data collection.

claim: Data sets were collected as a sequence of 6 s exposures per frame.
source: Data sets were then collected as a sequence of 6 s exposures per frame.
evidence: This describes the experimental data collection parameters.

claim: The dimensions of most microcrystals varied between 6 and 20 µm in length, 2 and 8 µm in width, and the thickness was approximately 100–200 nm.
source: The dimensions of most microcrystals varied between 6 and 20 µm in length, 2 and 8 µm in width, and the thickness was approximately 100–200 nm, in agreement with previous catalase crystal sizes (Dorset and Parsons, 1975b).
evidence: This is stated in the Figure 1 caption based on measurements of the crystals.

claim: A representative crystal approximately 200 nm thick showed a ratio of 8.4 × 10−3 for the maximum intensity to incident beam.
source: A representative crystal, which was approximately 200 nm thick, showed a ratio of 8.4 × 10−3 for the maximum intensity and 0.18 for the sum of all intensities, which are close to the previously reported values (Unwin and Henderson, 1975; Dorset and Parsons, 1975a), indicating that kinematical assumption is valid for these diffraction data.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data.

claim: A representative crystal approximately 200 nm thick showed a ratio of 0.18 for the sum of all intensities to incident beam.
source: A representative crystal, which was approximately 200 nm thick, showed a ratio of 8.4 × 10−3 for the maximum intensity and 0.18 for the sum of all intensities, which are close to the previously reported values (Unwin and Henderson, 1975; Dorset and Parsons, 1975a), indicating that kinematical assumption is valid for these diffraction data.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data.

claim: The measured intensity ratios are close to previously reported values, indicating that kinematical assumption is valid for these diffraction data.
source: A representative crystal, which was approximately 200 nm thick, showed a ratio of 8.4 × 10−3 for the maximum intensity and 0.18 for the sum of all intensities, which are close to the previously reported values (Unwin and Henderson, 1975; Dorset and Parsons, 1975a), indicating that kinematical assumption is valid for these diffraction data.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison to prior work and established theory.

claim: For the kinematical theory to apply, the ratios of strongest diffracted intensity to unscattered incident beam and sum of all diffracted intensities to incident beam must be low.
source: We quantified the dynamic scattering of the catalase crystals using the ratio of the strongest diffracted intensity to the unscattered incident beam (Unwin and Henderson, 1975), as well as the ratio of the sum of all diffracted intensities on an image to the incident beam intensity as described by Dorset and Parsons (1975a). For the kinematical theory to apply, these ratios must be low.
evidence: This is established theory cited from prior work.

claim: Data sets from five microcrystals were each integrated with MOSFLM followed by merging and scaling with POINTLESS and AIMLESS.
source: Data sets from five microcrystals were each integrated with MOSFLM (Leslie and Powell, 2007) followed by merging and scaling with POINTLESS (Evans, 2011) and AIMLESS (Evans and Murshudov, 2013).
evidence: This describes the data processing methodology used.

claim: All five crystals yielded comparable resolution but varied in data completeness.
source: All crystals yielded comparable resolution but varied in data completeness (Table 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Table 1.

claim: Crystal 4 was chosen for processing separately because it had a good compromise between resolution and completeness.
source: Crystal 4 was chosen for processing separately because it had a good compromise between resolution and completeness.
evidence: This explains the rationale for the data processing strategy.

claim: Phases were determined by molecular replacement as implemented in MOLREP with PDB ID: 3NWL as a search model.
source: The data sets were processed to a range of resolutions (Table 2) and phases were determined by molecular replacement (MR) as implemented in MOLREP (Vagin and Teplyakov, 1997) with PDB ID: 3NWL (Foroughi et al., 2011) as a search model.
evidence: This describes the phasing methodology used.

claim: Refinement was performed using PHENIX and REFMAC with electron scattering factors.
source: Following MR, refinement using PHENIX and REFMAC (Murshudov et al., 1997; Adams et al., 2010) with electron scattering factors was performed.
evidence: This describes the refinement methodology used.

claim: Merging data from multiple crystals did not have a significant effect on data completeness because the catalase crystals all orient on the grid with the c-axis parallel to the electron beam.
source: Merging data from multiple crystals did not have a significant effect on data completeness, because the catalase crystals all orient on the grid with the c-axis parallel to the electron beam (Table 2).
evidence: This is an observation and inference from the data in Table 2.

claim: Merging multiple crystals had a negative impact on the final refinement statistics, most likely due to non-isomorphism between crystals.
source: When comparing the statistics presented in Table 2, it was clear that merging multiple crystals had a negative impact on the final refinement statistics, most likely due to non-isomorphism between crystals, and therefore the multiple crystal data sets were disregarded.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of refinement statistics in Table 2.

claim: Crystals 1, 2, 3, and 5 were relatively isomorphous and their diffraction data merged well.
source: Crystals 1, 2, 3, and 5 were relatively isomorphous and their diffraction data merged well, but the completeness of this data set was low (∼62%), and we chose not to use it.
evidence: This is an observation from the data merging process.

claim: The completeness of the merged data set from crystals 1, 2, 3, and 5 was low at approximately 62%.
source: Crystals 1, 2, 3, and 5 were relatively isomorphous and their diffraction data merged well, but the completeness of this data set was low (∼62%), and we chose not to use it.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from data processing.

claim: The information content in the 3–3.2 Å resolution shell was too low for inclusion.
source: Close analysis indicated that the information content in the 3–3.2 Å resolution shell was too low for inclusion, which was not surprising as the crystals did not diffract well beyond 3.2 Å at high tilt angles.
evidence: This is an assessment of data quality based on analysis.

claim: The resolution was truncated to 3.2 Å yielding a final model with acceptable refinement statistics (Rwork/Rfree = 26.2%/30.8%) and geometry.
source: We therefore truncated the resolution to 3.2 Å yielding a final model with acceptable refinement statistics (Rwork/Rfree = 26.2%/30.8%) and geometry (Table 3, Figure 2A, Video 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the refinement process.

claim: The final 2mFobs-DFcalc density map shows well-defined density surrounding the final refined model with overall map CC = 92.3%.
source: The final 2mFobs-DFcalc density map shows well-defined density surrounding the final refined model (overall map CC = 92.3%), both around the backbone and the side-chains (Figure 2B, Video 2), without significant peaks in the mFobs-DFcalc difference density map (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a quantitative assessment of map quality with visual evidence in figures.

claim: The solvent channels between the tetramers in the crystal lattice show very little density.
source: Additionally, the solvent channels between the tetramers in the crystal lattice show very little density (Figure 2D), further evidence of the quality of the model and data.
evidence: This is an observation from the density maps shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The final structure of catalase at 3.2 Å resolution determined by MicroED agrees well with previously solved X-ray structures, with an RMSD of 0.358 Å between the MicroED structure and PDB ID: 3NWL.
source: The final structure of catalase at 3.2 Å resolution determined by MicroED agrees well with previously solved X-ray structures, with an RMSD of 0.358 Å and 0.440 Å between the MicroED structure and PDB ID: 3NWL (Foroughi et al., 2011) and PDB ID: 4BLC (Ko et al., 1999), respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison to prior structures.

claim: The final structure of catalase at 3.2 Å resolution determined by MicroED has an RMSD of 0.440 Å between the MicroED structure and PDB ID: 4BLC.
source: The final structure of catalase at 3.2 Å resolution determined by MicroED agrees well with previously solved X-ray structures, with an RMSD of 0.358 Å and 0.440 Å between the MicroED structure and PDB ID: 3NWL (Foroughi et al., 2011) and PDB ID: 4BLC (Ko et al., 1999), respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison to prior structures.

claim: The orientation of the crystals prevented the full sampling of reciprocal space leading to systematic incompleteness (missing wedge or missing cone).
source: The orientation of our crystals prevented the full sampling of reciprocal space leading to systematic incompleteness (missing wedge or missing cone).
evidence: This is an inference based on the crystal orientation and data collection geometry.

claim: Despite data incompleteness, the resulting maps are still expected to be good enough for proper interpretation.
source: While the incompleteness of data is significant, the resulting maps are still expected to be good enough for proper interpretation (Glaeser et al., 1989).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior theoretical work.

claim: Molecular replacement with a single monomeric chain instead of the complete tetramer yielded a strong solution with all four molecules successfully placed to recreate the complete tetramer.
source: First, the robustness of the MR solution was tested by repeating the MR with a single monomeric chain of PDB ID: 3NWL (Foroughi et al., 2011) instead of the complete tetramer that was used originally. Even with a single chain, a strong solution was found with all four molecules successfully placed to recreate the complete tetramer (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; top MOLREP contrast score = 35.8, where a score of >3.0 is considered a strong solution. An identical test with synchrotron X-ray data yielded a top score of 23.7).
evidence: This is a validation test result with quantitative scores.

claim: The top MOLREP contrast score for the single chain MR was 35.8, where a score of >3.0 is considered a strong solution.
source: Even with a single chain, a strong solution was found with all four molecules successfully placed to recreate the complete tetramer (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; top MOLREP contrast score = 35.8, where a score of >3.0 is considered a strong solution. An identical test with synchrotron X-ray data yielded a top score of 23.7).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the MR validation test.

claim: An identical test with synchrotron X-ray data yielded a top MOLREP score of 23.7.
source: Even with a single chain, a strong solution was found with all four molecules successfully placed to recreate the complete tetramer (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; top MOLREP contrast score = 35.8, where a score of >3.0 is considered a strong solution. An identical test with synchrotron X-ray data yielded a top score of 23.7).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison to X-ray data.

claim: When the data were phased with a poly-alanine model, the resulting maps show clear density beyond the model where the correct side-chains could be rebuilt.
source: We also phased the data with a poly-alanine model derived from PDB ID: 3NWL, and the resulting maps show clear density beyond the model where the correct side-chains could be rebuilt (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is a validation test result with visual evidence in the figure supplement.

claim: Autobuilding with Buccaneer yielded 2120 residues in 160 fragments.
source: In order to test the quality of the resulting maps following MR, autobuilding with Buccaneer (Cowtan, 2006) was performed and yielded 2120 residues in 160 fragments (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the autobuilding validation test.

claim: Out of the autobuilt residues, 1280 traced the correct backbone and 467 side-chains were correctly assigned.
source: Out of the built residues, 1280 traced the correct backbone and 467 side-chains were correctly assigned.
evidence: This is a quantitative assessment of autobuilding accuracy.

claim: Manual curation in Coot, exploiting the fourfold non-crystallographic symmetry, resulted in a nearly complete model indicating the maps initially produced from the data were of good quality.
source: Manual curation in Coot (Emsley et al., 2010), exploiting the fourfold non-crystallographic symmetry, resulted in a nearly complete model indicating the maps initially produced from our data were of good quality.
evidence: This is an inference based on the success of manual model building.

claim: The difference maps from the ∆181–185 model showed significant positive difference density corresponding to the deleted regions of the model.
source: Following refinement and simulated annealing, the resulting difference maps from the ∆181–185 model (Figure 3A) and ∆heme model (Figure 3C) both showed significant positive difference density corresponding to the deleted regions of the model.
evidence: This is a validation test result with visual evidence in Figure 3.

claim: The difference maps from the ∆heme model showed significant positive difference density corresponding to the deleted regions of the model.
source: Following refinement and simulated annealing, the resulting difference maps from the ∆181–185 model (Figure 3A) and ∆heme model (Figure 3C) both showed significant positive difference density corresponding to the deleted regions of the model.
evidence: This is a validation test result with visual evidence in Figure 3.

claim: Automated ligand identification using phenix.ligand_identification was able to correctly place two of the four heme groups present in the structure.
source: Additionally, automated ligand identification was performed on the ∆heme maps using phenix.ligand_identification (Terwilliger et al., 2006, 2007), and the program was able to correctly place two of the four heme groups present in the structure.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the automated ligand identification validation test.

claim: The validation test results indicate that the data do not suffer from bias introduced by the MR search model.
source: The results of these tests indicate that the data do not suffer from bias introduced by the MR search model.
evidence: This is an inference based on the validation test results.

claim: Bovine catalase binds four NADP cofactors, one per monomer through several side-chain interactions including F197.
source: Bovine catalase binds four NADP cofactors, one per monomer through several side-chain interactions including F197 (Kirkman and Gaetani, 1984; Fita and Rossmann, 1985).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior structural and biochemical work.

claim: In the NADP-free structure (PDB ID: 3RGP), F197 underwent a conformational change as it no longer interacted with NADP.
source: Recently, the structure of bovine catalase was solved lacking the NADP cofactor (PDB ID: 3RGP) (Purwar et al., 2011), and in the NADP-free structure F197 underwent a conformational change as it no longer interacted with NADP.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior structural work.

claim: The crystals used for MicroED analysis contain NADP.
source: The crystals used for our MicroED analysis do contain NADP.
evidence: This is stated based on the crystallization conditions and validated by the structural analysis.

claim: When analyzing the difference maps using the NADP-free structure as a search model, positive density was observed in the location expected for NADP although it appeared fragmented even at lower contour levels.
source: When analyzing the difference maps, positive density was observed in the location expected for NADP although it appeared fragmented even at lower contour levels (Figure 3E,G).
evidence: This is an observation from the difference maps shown in Figure 3.

claim: Maps from both MicroED and synchrotron X-ray diffraction appear fragmented around the NADP even at lower contour levels.
source: Maps from both MicroED and synchrotron X-ray diffraction appear fragmented around the NADP even at lower contour levels (Figure 3G,H).
evidence: This is a comparative observation from the maps shown in Figure 3.

claim: The difference maps for both the MicroED and X-ray synchrotron data suggest that F197 should change its orientation to assume its correct position for NADP binding.
source: The difference maps for both the MicroED and X-ray synchrotron data suggest that F197 should change its orientation to assume its correct position for NADP binding.
evidence: This is an inference based on analysis of the difference maps.

claim: The MicroED data is of sufficient quality to detect subtle differences among structures at atomic resolution.
source: These results demonstrate the MicroED data is of sufficient quality to detect subtle differences among structures at atomic resolution.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the validation tests showing detection of NADP and F197 conformational changes.

claim: At the current level of methodology with samples that suffer from missing data like catalase, MicroED produces lower quality maps than synchrotron X-ray diffraction.
source: At the current level of methodology with samples that suffer from missing data like catalase, MicroED produces lower quality maps than synchrotron X-ray diffraction.
evidence: This is an assessment based on comparison of map quality between MicroED and X-ray data.

claim: The catalase crystals used for MicroED were approximately 1000 times smaller in volume than those used at the synchrotron.
source: However, the catalase crystals used for MicroED were approximately 1000 times smaller in volume than those used at the synchrotron (Foroughi et al., 2011), and the resulting maps are still of high enough quality to determine the structure.
evidence: This is a calculation based on crystal dimensions reported in this work and the cited synchrotron study.

claim: The resulting MicroED maps are still of high enough quality to determine the structure despite being from much smaller crystals.
source: However, the catalase crystals used for MicroED were approximately 1000 times smaller in volume than those used at the synchrotron (Foroughi et al., 2011), and the resulting maps are still of high enough quality to determine the structure.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the successful structure determination.

claim: This is the second example where a single crystal was sufficient for structure determination by MicroED.
source: This is the second example where a single crystal was sufficient for structure determination by MicroED (Nannenga et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The continuous rotation method yields data similar in quality to X-ray diffraction allowing simple processing with existing X-ray data reduction software.
source: Moreover, the continuous rotation method yields data similar in quality to X-ray diffraction allowing simple processing with existing X-ray data reduction software and further accelerating structure analysis by MicroED (Nannenga et al., 2014).
evidence: This is demonstrated in this work and supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The resulting maps allow distinguishing between subtly different protein conformations and identifying small-molecule ligands such as NADP.
source: The resulting maps allow us to distinguish between subtly different protein conformations and to identify of small-molecule ligands such as NADP.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the validation tests with F197 and NADP.

claim: MicroED can be used as an alternative to X-ray crystallography using extremely small crystals for both mechanistic studies as well as structure-based drug design studies where small ligands are assayed.
source: This study shows that MicroED can be used as an alternative to X-ray crystallography using extremely small crystals for both mechanistic studies as well as structure-based drug design studies where small ligands are assayed.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the demonstrated capabilities of MicroED in this study.

claim: Catalase was recrystallized from a commercial aqueous suspension by first centrifuging the crystalline suspension and dissolving the pellet in 1.7 M NaCl.
source: Catalase was recrystallized from a commercial aqueous suspension of catalase (C100; Sigma–Aldrich, St. Louis, MO) by first centrifuging the crystalline suspension and dissolving the pellet in 1.7 M NaCl.
evidence: This describes the experimental crystallization procedure.

claim: All electron diffraction was performed on a FEI Tecnai F20 TEM operated at 200 kV.
source: All electron diffraction was performed on a FEI Tecnai F20 TEM operated at 200 kV with a selected area aperture (6 μm in diameter at the specimen) and data were collected with 4k × 4k TVIPS F416 CMOS cameras (15.6 μm pixel size).
evidence: This describes the experimental equipment and parameters.

claim: Diffraction data were collected with a frame rate of 1 frame per 6 s as the sample was continuously rotated from high to low tilt angle at approximately 0.09° s−1 (0.54°/frame).
source: Diffraction data were collected with a frame rate of 1 frame per 6 s as the sample was continuously rotated from high to low tilt angle at ∼0.09° s−1 (0.54°/frame) as described previously (Nannenga et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the data collection parameters.

claim: A data set of approximately 61° was collected from a single crystal.
source: A data set of approximately 61° was collected from a single crystal.
evidence: This describes the angular range of data collection.

claim: The RMSD between the MR solution from single monomer search and the original MR solution from complete tetramer search model was only 0.381 Å.
source: The RMSD between this MR solution and the original MR solution from complete tetramer search model was only 0.381 Å.
evidence: This is stated in the Figure 2—figure supplement 1 caption as a quantitative comparison.
